topic: Can satellite orbital configurations optimize ML-based QoS by reducing propagation delays for latency-sensitive traffic classes?
consensus_response: Satellite orbital configurations can optimize ML-based QoS by reducing propagation delays. Lower orbits like LEO minimize latency, while beamforming and ML algorithms dynamically adjust signal focus and path selection to reduce errors and interference, ensuring low latency and high throughput for latency-sensitive traffic.
reference_context: QoS mechanisms like RSVP-TE and ECMP have limitations in satellite networks, neglecting latency and jitter, but integrating real-time link data and ML can enhance QoS.
